---
title: "Exposure offsets"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

A count is inseparable from its opportunity window. For Nettle's country data, area is a proposed exposure: larger countries provide more geographic space in which languages are counted. An **offset** fixes the exposure coefficient rather than estimating it.

```{r}
#| label: load-nettle-offset
#| echo: true
path <- "data/nettle/nettle-1999-climate.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  nettle <- read.csv(path)
} else {
  url <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bodowinter/",
                "applied_statistics_book_data/master/nettle_1999_climate.csv")
  source_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  download.file(url, source_file, mode = "wb")
  stopifnot(digest::digest(source_file, "sha256", file = TRUE, serialize = FALSE) ==
    "3c5abfbec7b2132a9b81ee9a178cbd5559426578032b60c6c4ad74046898793b")
  raw <- read.csv(source_file)
  nettle <- data.frame(country = raw$Country, log10_population = raw$Population,
    log10_area_km2 = raw$Area, log_area_km2 = log(10) * raw$Area,
    mean_growing_season_months = raw$MGS, language_count = as.integer(raw$Langs))
}
stopifnot(nrow(nettle) == 74L)
```

If $A_i$ is area and $r_i$ is the expected language rate per unit area, then

$$
\lambda_i=A_i r_i,
$$

so

$$
\log\lambda_i=\log A_i+\log r_i
=\log A_i+\beta_0+\beta_1\operatorname{MGS}_i.
$$

The offset is $\log A_i$ with coefficient fixed at one.

```{r}
#| label: derive-and-fit-offset
#| echo: true
nettle$derived_log_area <- log(10) * nettle$log10_area_km2
stopifnot(max(abs(nettle$derived_log_area - nettle$log_area_km2)) < 1e-10)
fit <- glm(language_count ~ mean_growing_season_months + offset(derived_log_area),
           poisson(link = "log"), nettle)
nettle$fitted_count <- predict(fit, type = "response")
head(nettle[c("country", "language_count", "fitted_count")])
```

```{r}
#| label: offset-count-plot
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(nettle, aes(language_count, fitted_count)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey65", linewidth = .5) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, color = "#1F5A85") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Observed language count", y = "Fitted language count") +
  theme_classic()
```

The source `Area` column is base-10 logarithmic. A Poisson log link uses natural logarithms, hence the explicit conversion $\log A_i=\log(10)\log_{10}A_i$. Treating area as exposure assumes proportionality between expected count and area. Nettle's paper estimates the area coefficient, so this fixed-one version is a teaching model rather than a reproduced analysis.
